The real cost

A missed call
isn't a
minor thing.

When your phone rings and you can't answer, the caller has three options: leave a voicemail nobody listens to, try a competitor, or give up. Two of those three mean you lose the job.

Voicemail doesn't qualify leads. It doesn't tell you if it's a £50 call-out or a £1,200 full rewire. CallCatch does.

The questions
I get asked.

Real answers
Will the customer know it's a bot texting them?

The text says "Hi, on the tools, couldn't get to the phone." It reads exactly like you'd reply if you had ten seconds between jobs. Most customers don't notice, they just want their job sorted.

What if I'm somewhere with no signal?

Your CallCatch number lives in the cloud, not on your physical phone. As long as Twilio is up, missed calls still trigger the text-back. Your phone signal only matters for receiving the final lead summary, which lands the moment you're back in coverage.

Can I cancel anytime?

Yes. No contract, no notice period. During the free trial there's no card on file, I literally can't charge you. After the trial, WhatsApp me "cancel" and I deactivate your number same day.

What if the AI says something wrong to my customer?

The AI is very good at extracting name/postcode/job from a message, but it's not perfect. If a customer sends something confusing, the AI still passes you the raw text so you have full context. You always see the original message too.

How is this different from voicemail?

Voicemail is one-way and most callers don't leave one. CallCatch starts a real text conversation in seconds, captures structured info, and delivers it clean to your phone. Higher response rate, zero effort.

What happens after the 21-day trial?

Day 18 I'll WhatsApp you: "Worth continuing?" If yes, £45/mo, paid by bank transfer or Stripe. If no, I deactivate your number. No automatic charges, no surprise emails.
